method: Independent conservative extraction from complete original sessions. A candidate is retained only when the trajectory contains a concrete trigger, action/decision, observable verification or completion condition, explicit boundary, and direct source evidence. Overlapping/near-duplicate candidates were merged.

skills.skill: Repair a reactive UI by locating the rendering boundary that prevents framework initialization, moving stateful views into framework-owned components/stores, and explicitly initializing dynamically inserted trees.
skills.trigger: Interactive elements rendered through raw HTML injection do not respond or framework directives are inert.
actions: Inspect the render path and identify that x-html/raw strings bypass Alpine compilation.
Move screens and window/taskbar state into Alpine components/stores.
After dynamic insertion, call Alpine.initTree and then run icon replacement.
skills.verification: The direct evidence reports the click target working after explicit dimensions and pointer-event fixes, Alpine window content initializing, and feather replacement completing after Alpine.nextTick.
skills.scope_limit: Applies to Alpine-style reactive DOM insertion and this class of lifecycle bug; does not prescribe a framework-independent UI rewrite.

sources.evidence: The real remaining issue was pointer-events on the SVG children blocking the click, which is now fixed in CSS.
x-data inside x-html is dead HTML until you explicitly call Alpine.initTree(el). Added Alpine.nextTick(() => Alpine.initTree(el)) after the window opens.

skills.skill: Make UI process lifecycle idempotent: refuse duplicate process creation for an already-open window and attach cleanup to the window close lifecycle.
skills.trigger: Repeated open clicks create leaked process records, or closing a window leaves its process-manager entry alive.
actions: Add an onClose callback to the window entry.
Call terminateProcess from the close callback and capture stable store references for taskbar handlers.
skills.verification: The trajectory explicitly identifies the duplicate-create leak and missing cleanup, then reports both guards and onClose cleanup as fixed; it also reports the taskbar context fix.
skills.scope_limit: Applies to the observed window/process manager integration; it does not generalize to arbitrary resource lifetimes without an equivalent close event.

sources.evidence: Apps were calling createProcess() unconditionally on every open click ... leaking processes every click. Now each app guards with windows.isOpen() first.
windows.close() never called the app's cleanup ... Added an onClose callback to WindowEntry that the store calls on close.

skills.skill: Align static-site deployment configuration with the actual asset layout before deploying: disable an inferred build and serve the repository root when the build output would otherwise be empty.
skills.trigger: A deployment platform auto-detects a build directory that does not contain the site's root HTML/assets.
actions: Inspect package/build configuration and the actual asset tree.
Confirm whether the entry JavaScript has imports requiring bundling.
Set buildCommand to empty and outputDirectory to the root when justified, then deploy.
skills.verification: The trajectory reports production deployment success and gives a live URL after adding buildCommand "" and outputDirectory "."; it ties the fix to the observed dist/root mismatch.
skills.scope_limit: Specific to static hosting with this root-versus-dist failure mode; it does not imply that bundling should be disabled for projects with imports.

sources.evidence: main.js has no imports — esbuild bundling is unnecessary. The real issue was vercel.json has no buildCommand or outputDirectory ... serve the root directly.
Deployed successfully. ... Added "buildCommand": "" and "outputDirectory": "." to vercel.json.

skills.skill: Preserve a legacy rendering path while adding a framebuffer path by routing shared drawing through an abstraction and selecting the path from boot-time capability data.
skills.trigger: A kernel feature works through VGA text memory but must also run under UEFI/GOP without direct VGA writes.
actions: Parse the GOP capability from the Multiboot 2 tag.
Keep MB1/VGA fallback and MB2/GOP as separate boot paths.
Route shared printing/cell drawing through syscalls or the dual-path VGA abstraction and add the GOP object/build/run wiring.
skills.verification: The trajectory reports both headers retained, MB2/GOP primary plus MB1/VGA fallback, direct VGA writes removed from snake, and clean compilation/build checks.
skills.scope_limit: Applies to this boot/rendering compatibility boundary; it does not claim that every hardware path can share the same implementation without capability-specific code.

sources.evidence: Carries both headers ... MB2 ... and MB1 ... as the legacy fallback. Both entry paths converge at the same _start.
Removed all VGA_ADDR direct writes from snake ... All cell drawing goes through SYS_PUTCELL ... works on both VGA text and GOP.

skills.skill: Turn invalid domain selections into actionable diagnostics by reporting the exact attempted call, target type, rejection reason, and selectable alternatives in the thrown error.
skills.trigger: A query/property selector rejects a derived or non-persisted property and a generic exception does not explain how to correct it.
actions: Include the attempted method/property and argument shape.
Name the target model/type and why the selection is unsupported.
List selectable persisted alternatives and apply the same treatment to sibling invalid calls.
skills.verification: The trajectory reports the exact call, target type, reason, selectable properties, and matching treatment for the sibling get/zoom rejection; later evidence reports the full dal suite passing after the feature work.
skills.scope_limit: Applies to selector/query validation diagnostics; it does not replace the underlying feature implementation or authorize guessing support for computed lenses.

sources.evidence: Task 1 is done. The exception now reports the exact call, the target type, why it failed, and what is selectable.
All 89 dal.* tests pass (65 base + 15 zoom + 9 nested).

skills.skill: Validate an installable mobile app with complementary static and on-device evidence, and verify suspected findings before reporting them.
skills.trigger: A package review needs both manifest/code risk evidence and behavioral evidence that static inspection cannot reveal.
actions: Scan permissions, trackers, network hosts, version and recipe consistency.
Install and exercise the app when device access is available.
Separate confirmed findings from unavailable tests and re-check apparent positives before posting a factual report.
skills.verification: The session reports successful launch and interaction for multiple apps, distinguishes a transitive firebase-encoders false positive from active trackers, and reports the self-updater only after observing it on-device.
skills.scope_limit: Applies to the observed F-Droid/mobile review workflow; it does not treat static or device evidence as interchangeable, and it stops device claims when access is denied.

sources.evidence: Important catch — that Firebase was a false positive: precise inspection shows only firebase-encoders ... no active tracker.
Launched cleanly ... It works — a clean offline expense tracker ... The add-expense dialog works fully.
ScenePeek shows an Update available dialog ... That is a built-in self-updater — an F-Droid anti-feature concern that static analysis wouldn't surface.
